name: Syncthing-GTK
description: Auto-downloads the Syncthing daemon binary, extracts with zero hash/sig, chmod +x, runs it.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Syncthing-GTK extracts the daemon archive and stages it executable without payload verification.
limitations: Newly retrieved/recovered source snapshot; this is not historical source re-verification. Released artifact behavior and external framework enforcement remain unverified.

original_evidence.text: | Syncthing-GTK | https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing-gtk (archived/deprecated) | Python2/GTK | Y | auto chk/dl/inst (of the managed Syncthing **daemon**, not of Syncthing-GTK itself) | Y — downloads a daemon binary archive from GitHub and writes it to disk with executable permission; the app subsequently launches it as a subprocess | HTTPS via GLib/GIO (`Gio.File.new_for_uri`) to api.github.com; TLS validation left at GIO/glib-networking default (ENFORCED) — no bypass code found in the downloader path itself | N (relies on GitHub API JSON + release asset, no separate signed manifest) | none (no checksum/signature check of the downloaded archive before extraction) | `syncthing_gtk/stdownloader.py`: `ST_URL = "https://api.github.com/repos/syncthing/syncthing/releases"` (line 22); `get_version()`/`_cb_read_latest()` (lines 107-224) picks the newest compatible release and asset URL from the GitHub API JSON with no signature/hash check; `download()` (lines 227-241) fetches `self.dll_url` via `Gio.File.new_for_uri(...).read_async`; `_open_archive`/`_extract` (lines 284-352) extract the `syncthing`/`syncthing.exe` binary from the tar/zip and `os.fchmod(output.fileno(), 0o755)` (line 341) makes it executable — no hash/signature verification anywhere in this file. `syncthing_gtk/app.py:535-537,639-641,2147-2191` stage the new binary as `<path>.new`, then on next start swap it into place as `self.config["syncthing_binary"]` and launch it (`app.py:477` `cmdline = [self.config["syncthing_binary"], ...]`), i.e. an unverified downloaded binary is executed. Note: an unrelated `ssl.CERT_NONE` bypass exists in `syncthing_gtk/iddialog.py:97-108`, but that is for loading QR-code images from the local daemon's self-signed HTTPS API, not the updater. |
